modelTitle: How Per-Seat Video Plans Scale in the Enterprise.
modelParagraphs: Synthesia sells enterprise AI video on a per-seat SaaS model: corporate plans seat users at tiers from tens to hundreds of dollars per creator per month, with video minutes and avatar features metered on top. The buyer is L&D and corporate communications — training, onboarding and explainers produced in 140+ languages without camera crews — which is why the platform's claimed ~90% Fortune 100 penetration converts into durable, contracted revenue.

Enterprise add-ons deepen the mix: custom brand avatars, one-click translation, SOC 2-grade security and API access for embedding video generation into customer products. The January 2026 $200M Series E led by GV, with Nvidia participating, valued the company at $4 billion — roughly double the prior round — as it reportedly targets $200M ARR within the year.
revenueMix: Tiered creator seats for enterprise L&D and communications teams.
Custom avatars, translation, security and API packages.
Video generation embedded into customer products via API.

faqs.a: Synthesia is estimated at roughly $150 million of ARR in 2026, up from the company-confirmed $100 million in April 2025. The company reportedly expects to cross $200 million within the year. That implies about $12.5 million of monthly recurring revenue.
April 2025, announced by the company alongside Adobe's investment. Synthesia had reportedly turned down a $3 billion takeover offer from Adobe around that period.

Per-seat enterprise SaaS: tiered creator plans for L&D and communications teams, with metered video minutes and enterprise add-ons — custom avatars, 140+ language translation, security certifications and API access for product embedding.
$4 billion after a $200 million Series E led by GV (Google Ventures) with Nvidia participating, closed in January 2026 — nearly double the $2.1 billion valuation from the prior $180 million round.

faqs.q: How Many Big Companies Use Synthesia?
faqs.a: Roughly 90% of the Fortune 100, including Microsoft, UBS and Ford, per 2026 reporting. The enterprise base is the core of the business model: training and communication video built by employees on contracted seats.
